$comment: The webhook contract between the inbound-mail Email Worker (deploy/pulumi/src/platform/inbound-mail-worker.js) and the BFF (frontends/ui/src/lib/inbound-mail/contract.ts, the route under /api/internal/signed/). The Worker posts the buffered message to `path` on the app origin (the origin of WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI), signs `signedComponents` (RFC 9421, `signatureAlgorithm`, expires = created + signatureLifetimeSeconds, label `signatureLabel`) over an RFC 9530 Content-Digest, and reads the answer by `cases`: a 2xx is accepted, a 4xx carrying `verdictHeader: verdictReject` is bounced with `rejectText`, and everything else makes it throw so the sending server retries. Neither side imports this file at runtime (the Worker is one dependency-free module; the BFF's image has no shared/): each states the values in code and a spec on each side holds them to this file (contract.spec.ts; inbound-mail-worker.spec.ts). The signature itself is pinned by shared/inbound-mail-signature.json. ADR-0135; the bounce set is DECISION D5.
rejectText: This message could not be delivered: the address is unknown or no longer valid. Help: https://piloti.at/e-mail-eingang/ Privacy: https://piloti.at/datenschutz/
unknownAddressText: Unknown address: this message was not delivered.

envelopeEncoding.$comment: How the Worker writes an SMTP envelope address into envelopeToHeader and envelopeFromHeader, and how the BFF reads it back. Every byte of the address's UTF-8 form outside 0x21-0x7E, and '%' itself, is written as %XX (uppercase hex), so decodeURIComponent restores it exactly; an ASCII address without '%' passes unchanged. A null reverse-path (an empty envelope sender, as on a bounce) is written as nullSender, never as an empty header.

limitsNote: maxRawMessageBytes (26 MiB: Cloudflare's 25 MiB inbound cap plus headroom) is the largest body the BFF accepts; a larger signed Content-Length is answered 413 + reject before a byte is read. edgeMaxBodyBytes (27 MiB) is the edge's ceiling for every signed route (deploy/pulumi src/constants.ts SIGNED_INTERNAL_ROUTE), at or above it, so a real mail meets the BFF's bounce and never the edge's bare 413. workerTimeoutMs is how long the Worker waits for an answer before it throws.

cases.note: held, or dropped as an auto-reply
a closed project HOLDS its mail (RT-X13)
unknown or revoked token, deleted project, office switched off
a 404 without the verdict is a misrouted URL or a proxy, never the sender's fault
the edge's own 413 (over edgeMaxBodyBytes, or no Content-Length)
signature refused: our key is wrong, not the mail
over a rate limit or byte cap
a redirect is never followed (redirect: manual)
